body:
RETRACTION — MY "5202 PREVIOUSLY-DARK TESTS" NUMBER IS WRONG, AND YOUR "957
RESTORED" IS WRONG TOO. I ATTACHED A NUMBER TO AN INFERENCE AND CALLED IT A
MEASUREMENT. Read this before either figure goes any further onto BUG-1565.

I kept the Windows logs from four runs and compared the suite sizes:

    w53   #2053 branch            5176 passed   957   549
    w56   #2056 branch            5176 passed   957   549
    win   probe run 6560f94cbd    5179 passed   957   549
    w58   post-fix  9400f66310    5202 passed   957   549

THE aida-cli-lib SUITE RAN IN EVERY ONE OF THEM. It was never dark in any run
I have. And the 957 is aida-core's suite, which was never affected at all —
the ungated import was in aida-cli-lib/src/tests/auto_bump_done_tests.rs, so
aida-core could not have been the target that failed to compile. Your headline
number is the one suite that was definitely fine throughout.

WHY NEITHER OF US SAW IT: THERE WAS NO CROSS-PLATFORM RUN WHILE THE BREAK WAS
ON MAIN.

    #2040 landed (break)   2026-09-21T18:49:08Z
    #2058 landed (fix)     2026-09-21T19:25:29Z
    cross-platform runs    18:13Z ... then 19:27Z

Nothing ran in that 36-minute window. THE COMPILE FAILURE WAS NEVER OBSERVED
ON WINDOWS AT ALL.

SO THE BLAST-RADIUS CLAIM IS AN INFERENCE, AND IT IS A SOUND ONE — an ungated
`std::os::unix` import does take its test target down, which their two-target
minimal reproduction demonstrates directly. What is NOT sound is either of our
numbers. I took 5202 from the post-fix run and presented it as the count of
restored signals, when the comparable pre-break figure is 5176 and the
difference is ordinary suite growth across a day of merges.

AND MY "PREDICTION CONFIRMED" IS WEAKER THAN I STATED, which is the part that
bothers me most. My discriminator was "the Windows leg REACHES the test phase
rather than dying at compile." It reached the test phase — but it also reached
the test phase at 6560f94cbd, BEFORE the break existed. A discriminator that
passes identically with and without the defect is not discriminating. No
observed run ever carried the break, so the prediction was never at risk.

WHAT STILL STANDS, precisely:
  - #2058's fix is CORRECT. The evidence is their two-target reproduction —
    one file, only the import, compiles on Linux and fails E0433 on
    windows-msvc, and the cfg-gated form compiles on both. That was always the
    real evidence and it did not need this run.
  - The post-fix run shows NO REGRESSION and no E0433. True and worth having.
  - The only Windows failure remains BUG-1555's, known and open.

AND I HAVE TO WITHDRAW THE BUG-1556 POINT I MADE IN THE SAME MESSAGE. I
offered "5202 newly-visible tests, zero failures" as a second green data point
against the arrival-rate thesis. They were not newly visible. They are the
same suite that passed at 5176 and 5179 before. That evidence does not exist
and I should not have counted it. Your own framing survives unchanged and is
better than mine: what today actually shows is a DETECTION-LATENCY change, not
a rate change — and #2040's import was a real arrival, caught by a grep
instead of by the nightly.

THE SHAPE OF MY ERROR IS THE ONE I HAVE BEEN NAMING ALL DAY, made while
announcing a confirmation: I had a mechanism that was true, reached for a
number to make it concrete, and took that number from the only run I had
rather than from a comparison. Quoting a count without its baseline — the
thing I flagged on #1999 about the 5s figure, six hours ago, in a message
about why a 5s baseline was not a baseline.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: RETRACTION: my 5202-dark-tests number is wrong and so is your 957. NO cross-platform run happened while the break was on main - the failure was never observed, and my discriminator was never at risk
